messages:
pooja: Quick Q — can we add a lightweight per-route suppression policy in the console? we're getting a ton of tenant churn alerts that are basically the same failure, and paging on each is noisy.

alex: +1. do you mean a UI toggle or an API field?

pooja: both ideally. UI toggle to set a route-level "quiet_backoff" and an API param so infra can set via service config. thinking something like: quiet_backoff = {window_sec: 300, multiplier: 2, max_repeats: 5} so repeated hits suppress after X but still escalate if sustained.

maria: I worry about masking real incidents. need an escape hatch: evaluate by error_budget or unique_failure_signature. if different signatures show up, don't suppress.

chris: Agreed. Also sampling should be weighted by tenant SLA tier. for free tiers we can sample more aggressively. for enterprise tenants we should route to full fanout.

julia: Another idea — use velocity-based suppression. if alerts are >N/min but duplicate fingerprint, suppress and create a single aggregated alert with count+top-5-logs. keeps ops informed but quiet.

pooja: Exactly. Proposed scoring: suppression_score = min(1, duplicates_in_window / threshold) * (1 - error_budget_ratio) * tenant_weight. If score > 0.8 -> suppress to aggregated channel.

alex: Can we do that without changing DB schema? prefer config-only change that composes with existing notify-fanout logic. maybe add a new notify_route param: "aggregation_policy": "quiet_backoff_v1" and push the policy into notify service to evaluate at fanout time.

maria: Also need telemetry: per-route suppressed_count, suppressed_tenants, last_unfold_time. Without metrics this will be impossible to tune.

chris: +1 for metrics. add events for suppressed->unfold transitions so playbooks can surface.

pooja: Rough API payload I sketched for the console (open to bikeshedding):

```json
{
  "route_id": "r_123",
  "notify_config": {
    "aggregation_policy": "quiet_backoff_v1",
    "policy_params": {
      "window_sec": 300,
      "multiplier": 2,
      "max_repeats": 5,
      "min_error_budget_pct": 0.1
    }
  }
}
```

julia: That looks good. what about per-tenant overrides? e.g., enterprise always false.

pooja: plan is per-route default + optional per-tenant override table. console will show a small badge on the SLO card: "Quieting: on/off" and a link to view suppressed events.

alex: Implementation notes: notify-service already computes fingerprint and fanout. we can add a pre-fanout step that consults the aggregation policy and returns one of {fanout_all, aggregate, drop} plus metadata. low-risk to implement behind a feature flag.

chris: rollout idea — start with UI-only: let users preview suppression estimates (like "would suppress 75% of alerts in last 7d"). then opt-in per-route. don't flip on globally.

maria: Strongly +1 to preview mode. also add a dry-run telemetry mode that surfaces false negatives (alert that would have been suppressed but wasn't because of override) so we can tune thresholds.

pooja: I can mock console UI and a preview query. who can update notify-service contract? alex?

alex: I can take a PR to add the new field and a feature flag gate. will add an integration test to cover aggregate vs fanout.

sre-bot: FYI: deploy-bot triggered canary for notify-service at sha abc123 10m ago.

deploy-bot: Canary passed in us-west-2, 2/3 workers.

julia: one more edgecase: multi-signal incidents where multiple SLOs spike simultaneously. aggregation should prefer grouping by fingerprint only within the same signal type. we don't want to merge CPU and request_error spikes even if they co-occur.

chris: Good call. policy should accept allowed_signal_types list. default to route.signal_type.

maria: Also add RBAC control for console toggle — security will want tenant admins only.

pooja: I'll open a design doc with API contract, UI mock, and telemetry list. will include sample queries for preview and dry-run.

alex: cool. timeline?

pooja: aiming for a small pilot next week behind FF. design doc by EOD today.

maria: Ping me on the doc, I'll add telemetry metrics.

chris: I'll sketch the pre-fanout flow and the unit tests.

julia: I'll do the UI badge and preview page.

pooja: Thanks team :pray: this should cut a lot of noise for oncall while keeping us safe.

sre-bot: Note: created ticket #INF-2291 for follow-up and rollout checklist.
